| 📍 **[q-0037.0017](docs/questions/q-0037.0017-what-is-a-session-to-the-harness-and-which-mechanism-keeps-its-lifecycle.md)** · What is a session to the harness, and which mechanism keeps its lifecycle? |
|---|

Nothing deletes them. Today a row is written once and changed forever after, never removed, and the format says so on purpose. The one thing the history buys turned out to be more than I said two replies ago, so I correct that first.

**What an old row is for.** The desktop app names a conversation by one id in every process it starts, and the hook registers the session under that id. So a conversation you reopen a day later finds its own row, turns it running again, keeps its position and is told no new recall is needed. That is a real use, and it covers the desktop host too, not the terminal alone.[^1] Everything older than a reopen could plausibly reach, which is days, buys nothing: the account of what each session did is its record under `docs/sessions/`, and the wake prints the rest into every session's context for no reader.

**The shape with the fewest parts.** A row lives while its session could still come back, and the wake removes it after that. One constant, one more step in the wake, which already walks every row to end the silent ones. The wake's read lists running sessions only. The conclude, the silence rule and the carry-over stay as they are. Seven days is my estimate of how long a reopen stays likely, and it is yours to lower or raise. I settled it as the method asks and stop here to show it before touching the format or the script. (🐛 self-improvement=a rule)

🧩 **Proposed rule — [QUESTION-FORMAT.md](.agents/skills/questions/QUESTION-FORMAT.md) · The sessions folder**

> What removes a row: a wake removes each ended row whose session has not returned within seven days, since a conversation the host reopens finds its row under the same id until then. The wake's read lists running sessions only.

The maintain pass's rule that commits rows a wake ended in other sessions' files will read *ended or removed*, a wording change that follows the rule above. The script change sits in the wake: a removal beside the silence rule, and the report's session list narrowed to running rows. The 125 rows now in the folder go with the first wake after it lands.

✋ Ended session rows removed by the wake after seven days, the wake listing running sessions only, in place of rows kept for good.

Yes from you, and I mint the ticket under this question and carry it through plan, implement and verify.

| ⚖️ Decisions |
|---|
| Ended rows removed after seven days by the wake, the wake listing running sessions only; or another window than seven days |

[^1]: The host table in `questions.py`: the desktop app keeps its own id for the conversation in every process it starts, 2026-10-09 and 2026-10-10.
